macros.name: greadlist
macros.doc: The macro \greadlist makes global assignments and therefore, enables the use of ⟨macro-list⟩ outside of the group where \greadlist has been executed.

macros.name: ignoreemptyitems
macros.doc: For empty items of the list (i.e., those list items defined by two consecutive parsing delimiters) to be ignored, we must, before invoking \readlist, execute the macro \ignoreemptyitems .

macros.name: itemtomacro
macros.doc: The \itemtomacro⟨macro-list⟩[index]⟨macro⟩ assigns to the ⟨macro⟩ the item designated by ⟨macro-list⟩[index]. The ⟨macro⟩ thus defined is purely expandable provided that the tokens in the items are expandable.

macros.name: listlen
macros.doc: The macro \listlen⟨macro-list⟩[⟨index⟩] requires 2 expansions in order to give the number of items in the list specified by the ⟨index⟩.

macros.name: nestdepth
macros.doc: The ⟨depth⟩ of nesting is contained in the purely expandable macro \nestdepth.

macros.name: readlist
macros.doc: To read the list of items, the \readlist⟨macro-list⟩{⟨list⟩} should be called. In so doing, the ⟨list⟩ is read and the items are stored in a macro, denoted ⟨macro-list⟩ which therefore acts as a table with the items of the ⟨list⟩.

macros.name: setsepchar
macros.doc: The default parsing separator is the comma and if we want change it, we must do so before reading a list of items, with the definition \setsepchar{⟨parsing-separator⟩}.

macros.name: showitems
macros.doc: For purposes of debugging, the macro \showitems⟨macro-list⟩ includes all items from a list, while the star version displays these items “detokenized.”
